# Conclusion

Over nine years, *Sasa* expanded by a net +19% on the study slope, a substantial change in alpine vegetation. Establishment was most strongly associated with distance from existing patches, and environmentally suitable area far exceeded the occupied area, suggesting that the current distribution is limited by dispersal rather than by habitat availability, with snowmelt timing shaping where establishment is most likely along the fronts. Projections conditioned on the observed decade place approximately 4,900–5,700 m² of establishment by 2030 in snowbed communities adjoining current patches; therefore, monitoring and removal can be targeted at patch fronts. Ground-based time-lapse imagery makes such process-level projection possible at the meter scale at which alpine vegetation changes.
